measurement_policy.baseline_selection: baseline-six.json and baseline-big.json; excludes the earlier baseline-small getrusage-floor captures
measurement_policy.extern_marker_counts: extern-marker helper entries need not decrease when work inside the miss path is removed
measurement_policy.memory: MiB; actual native Linux VmHWM. Stage peaks are cumulative, not isolated stage allocations. RSS is sampled in the compiler.
measurement_policy.missing_call_counts: null means unavailable, unobserved or optimized out; it does not mean zero
measurement_policy.profiles: selected exact GNU gprof flat-profile call counts only; manifests record PG -O1 -fno-inline flags. PG times and percentages are excluded
measurement_policy.seconds: serialized unprofiled -O2 timing captures; total includes compiler overhead outside named stages

remaining_limits: TY closure validation remains outside R1–R6: it walks all HIR items; each HIR closure count reaches parse closure/child counts that scan parse nodes, including bodies with no closures. TY can therefore remain superlinear.

The impl candidate index narrows lookup to K qualified candidates. L repeated queries still have O(L×K×log K) worst-case candidate iteration, plus semantic/header matching, because each next-candidate step uses upper-bound search. Workloads where query and candidate counts grow together remain superlinear.

The mutable-exclusivity preflight makes bodies with no actual Loan/LoanMut rows linear in P. Loan-bearing bodies retain the ordered write-by-path comparisons, O(W×P), and the existing liveness analysis.

The measured long workload remains loan-bearing. Its residual Meiya pair scans are not removed by the no-loan preflight; that narrower bound is covered by borrowck_mutable_preflight_smoke.fk. Statement indexing still removes the earlier full path scans from statement queries.

This checkpoint measures these generated workloads once in a serialized environment. It does not establish a universal twofold scaling bound or change conservative language/borrow-analysis boundaries.
